# Independent subscription application

Source: [Next.js SaaS Starter](https://github.com/nextjs/saas-starter/tree/6e33e58b1e553a41fe22e6b941a7229a002de361)
(MIT; included in `LICENSE`). `provenance.json` pins the commit, dependency
versions, and SHA-256 of the preparation patch.

Run `npm run test:adoption` from AutoPatch with Node.js 24, Git, pnpm, OpenSSL,
and internet access. The test downloads a disposable checkout and retains its
report, exact migration patch, runtime observations, and machine timings.

- `compatibility.patch` is **manual preparation**, not generated by AutoPatch.
  It removes deprecated `baseUrl`, declares CSS side-effect imports, uses generated
  Next.js route types, and adapts Drizzle relations to the pinned release candidate.
  It strengthens library checking rather than suppressing errors.
- `before.json`, `after.json`, and `bindings.json` describe an **authored local
  helper rename**, `getStripePrices` → `listStripePrices`. No upstream Stripe
  release is implied. The helper and its pricing-page caller already exist upstream.
- `check.mjs` runs the existing helper and real Stripe SDK against loopback HTTPS,
  replacing only the external transport destination. Literal expectations verify
  the request, API-version header, and returned price values before and after.

The preparation requires experimental Drizzle `1.0.0-rc.5-ab785fc`. The test does
not establish database, authentication, checkout, or production compatibility.
It adds one prepared-application scenario, separate from the curated corpus.
[Recorded results and limits](../../../docs/adoption-check.md).
